#Part A — Creating Vectors and List
# Question #1:
```{r}
# A factory has a census of its workers. There are 50 workers in total.

# a. Create a vector for the workers' ages
age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

cat("a. Workers' ages:\n")
print(age)

# b. How many data points?
cat("\nb. Number of data points:\n")
print(length(age))   # 50

# c. Minimum and maximum
cat("\nc. Minimum and maximum age:\n")
print(min(age))      # 17
print(max(age))      # 61

# d. 13th to 18th and 33rd to 35th elements
cat("\nd. 13th to 18th and 33rd to 35th elements:\n")
print(age[c(13:18, 33:35)])   # 27 22 37 34 19 20 33 41 53

# e. All elements except the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th
cat("\ne. All except the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements:\n")
print(age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)])

# f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th and 44th elements to 0
age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0

cat("\nf. After changing the 4th, 14th, 24th and 44th elements to 0:\n")
print(age)
```
# Question #2:
```{r}
# Question #2:
# R has actually lots of built-in datasets.
# For example, the rivers data "gives the lengths (in miles) of 141 "major"
# rivers in North America, as compiled by the US Geological Survey".
# Use data(rivers)

data(rivers)

# a. Individual statistics

cat("a. Individual statistics:\n")
cat("Length:", length(rivers), "\n")      # 141
cat("Sum:", sum(rivers), "\n")            # 83357
cat("Mean:", mean(rivers), "\n")          # 591.1844
cat("Median:", median(rivers), "\n")      # 425
cat("Variance:", var(rivers), "\n")       # 243908.4
cat("Standard deviation:", sd(rivers), "\n")  # 493.8708
cat("Minimum:", min(rivers), "\n")        # 135
cat("Maximum:", max(rivers), "\n")        # 3710

# b. All results in one vector

rivers_stats <- c(
  length = length(rivers),
  sum = sum(rivers),
  mean = mean(rivers),
  median = median(rivers),
  var = var(rivers),
  sd = sd(rivers),
  min = min(rivers),
  max = max(rivers)
              )

cat("\nb. All results in one vector (rivers_stats):\n")
print(round(rivers_stats, 1))
```
# Question 3:
```{r}
# The table below gives the 25 most powerful celebrities and their annual pay
# as ranked by the editions of Forbes magazine and as listed on the Forbes.com
# website.

# a. Create vectors according to the table

power_ranking <- 1:25

celebrity_name <- c("Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2",
                    "Tiger Woods", "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent",
                    "Cast of the Sopranos", "Dan Brown", "Bruce Springsteen",
                    "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", "Paul McCartney",
                    "George Lucas", "Elton John", "David Letterman",
                    "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt",
                    "Peter Jackson", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Lenon",
                    "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant")

pay <- c(67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88, 55, 44, 55,
         40, 233, 34, 40, 47, 75, 25, 39, 45, 32, 40, 31)

cat("a. Vectors created from the table:\n")
print(length(power_ranking))   # 25
print(length(celebrity_name))  # 25
print(length(pay))             # 25

# b. Modify J.K. Rowling's power ranking to 15 and pay to 90

power_ranking[19] <- 15
pay[19] <- 90

cat("\nb. J.K Rowling's new power ranking and pay:\n")
print(power_ranking[19])       # 15
print(pay[19])                 # 90

```
# Question #4:
```{r}
# Create a list of ten vegetables
vegetables <- c("carrots", "broccoli", "spinach", "cabbage", "tomato",
                "potato", "onion", "eggplant", "squash", "okra")

cat("a. List of ten vegetables:\n")
print(vegetables)

# 1. Add 2 vegetables after the last one
vegetables <- append(vegetables, c("cucumber", "kangkong"))

cat("\nb. After adding 2 vegetables at the end:\n")
print(vegetables)

# How many datapoints?
cat("\nc. Number of datapoints:\n")
print(length(vegetables))

# 3. Add 4 vegetables after index 5
vegetables <- append(vegetables, c("lettuce", "radish", "pechay", "corn"), after = 5)

cat("\nd. After adding 4 vegetables after index 5:\n")
print(vegetables)

# 4. How many datapoints now?
cat("\ne. Number of datapoints now:\n")
print(length(vegetables))
```
